examples.text: It certainly appears difficult to reconcile with known facts the opinion maintained by [Carl] Linnæus and by [Thomas] Pennant, which is, indeed, a very prevalent one, that all the tribes of tellurian animals now existing have descended from a stock that was preserved in the ark of Noah.

glosses: Of a planet, being composed primarily of silicate rocks or metals; see also terrestrial planet.

examples.text: The tellurian mineral from Goldfield, Nevada, described originally as goldfieldite by Ransome (1909), was proven to be tellurian tennantite by X-ray powder diffraction (Thompson 1946).

glosses: Alternative spelling of tellurion (“instrument used to show how the rotation of the Earth on its axis and its orbit around the Sun cause day and night and the seasons”).

examples.text: The Second Part of this Orrery I call a Tellurian, [...] becauſe it ſhews moſt accurately and evidently all the Phœnomena ariſing from the Annual and Diurnal Motions of the Earth, in a Terreſtrial Globe full Three Inches in a Diameter; upon which all the Parts of the terraqueous Surface are diſtinctly delineated, [...]

glosses: Alternative letter-case form of Tellurian (“inhabitant of the planet Earth”).

glosses: Que pertenece o concierne al planeta Tierra.
Procedente o nativo de la Tierra.
Que pertenece o concierne al telurismo (influencia del suelo o la tierra natal en la cultura humana).

Se dice de una tendencia literaria de América Latina que, durante la primera mitad del siglo XX, enfatizó la conexión con la tierra y el entorno rural o selvático. Se manifestó fundamentalmente en la novela, con autores como José Eustasio Rivera, Rómulo Gallegos y Ricardo Güiraldes, entre muchos otros.
